117707.name: Congregation Tzemach Tzedek
117707.note: Cleveland Jewish News (13 July 2011, Rabbi Zalman Kazen's obituary): 'The couple came to Cleveland in 1953 at the request of Lubavicher Rebbe Menachem Mendel Schneerson. While applying for a High Holiday position at what would become Zemach Zedek, he realized he was related to the Madorsky family, who founded the congregation (then known commonly as Nusach Ari Shul). Shortly after Zemach Zedek moved to Cleveland Heights in 1957, Rabbi Kazen bought his home on Glenmont Road, which served as Cleveland's original Chabad house. When Zemach Zedek's rabbi moved to Wickliffe, Rabbi Kazen was chosen to lead the congregation.' The CJN (3 July 2014): the Kazens 'brought the Chabad-Lubavitch movement to Cleveland in 1953'; Rabbi Kazen 'served as spiritual leader for more than 50 years'; Rabbi Mordechai Mendelson 'took over as Congregation Zemach Zedek's spiritual leader after the passing of Rabbi Kazen in 2011'. The year is the Kazens' arrival; the congregation itself (the Nusach Ari Shul) is older, its founding year not found. Now 1922 Lee Road; the listing still names Rabbi Zalman Kazen.

117708.name: Chabad of Cleveland
117708.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'When Rabbi Leibel Alevsky and his wife, Devorah, were sent to Cleveland in 1972 by Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson to establish the first Chabad house in Cleveland and eastern Ohio'; 'We started our activities that summer at the Case Western Reserve Hillel House,' while living with the Kazens in Cleveland Heights; 'there was no official Chabad building until the original Chabad House of Cleveland opened at 2004 S. Green Road in South Euclid in 1972.' The CJN (24 April 2026, Rabbi Alevsky's obituary): 'The 1972 opening of the Chabad house of Cleveland on South Green Road in South Euclid'. The CJN (26 April 2001): ground broken for the mikvah and the Waxman Chabad Center on South Green Road in Beachwood (now 2479 S Green Road); 'After the new Waxman Chabad Center opens, the old Chabad House will be torn down'. The 2004 S. Green Road building now houses the kosher pantry and the Russian shul.

earlier.where: the original Chabad House of Cleveland, 2004 S. Green Road, South Euclid

6057204.name: Cleveland Kosher Food Pantry
6057204.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'The Kosher Food Bank, a member of the Greater Cleveland Food Bank, began in the Zemach Zedek building in Cleveland Heights in 1974 in response to the large influx of Russian Jews. It is now located at the original Chabad House of Cleveland in South Euclid'. The CJN (21 Jan 2011): 'The kosher pantry, formerly known as the Russian/Kosher Foodbank, opened its doors more than 30 years ago when Shula and Rabbi Zalman Kazen launched it'. A department of Semach Sedek Shul (119647) on chabad.org; its listing went up Aug 21 2023. Now 2004 S Green Road.

earlier.where: the Zemach Zedek building, Lee Road, Cleveland Heights

119647.name: Semach Sedek Shul
119647.note: The Russian synagogue of the Kazens' Russian Immigrant Aid Society. Cleveland Jewish News (13 July 2011): 'The Kazens formed the Russian Immigrant Aid Society (R.I.A.S.) in the early 1970s'. The CJN (10 April 2003): 'Walk into Semek Sedek R.I.A.S. (Russian Immigrant Aid Society) Synagogue'; 'The home of Semek Sedek is a humble, storefront building located at 1922 Lee Road in Cleveland Heights'; 'After two decades of running the Aid Society single-handedly, the Kazens were recently joined by a young Chabad couple'. The CJN (3 July 2014): at the original Chabad House in South Euclid, 'A minyan for the Bukharian Jews, from Asian Russia, is held there every Saturday, directed by Rabbi Marozov.' No exact year: 'early 1970s'. Now 2004 South Green Road.

earlier.where: a storefront building at 1922 Lee Road, Cleveland Heights

117537.name: Chabad of Beachwood
117537.note: Rabbi Sholom Ber Chaikin's congregation. Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'In 1981, Rabbi Alevsky decided the Chabad House needed a pulpit rabbi, as the community had grown to more than 50 people. So Rabbi Sholom Ber Chaikin was brought in from London to serve as the Chabad's spiritual leader and halachic authority – a position he still holds.' The CJN's list the same day: 'Waxman Chabad Center, Beachwood Rabbi Sholom Ber and Sheindl Chaikin'. The CJN (15 March 2001): 'Chabad of Beachwood program director Yossi Marozov'; 'The current Beachwood structure will be demolished and a brand new building put in its place'; the CJN (26 April 2001) calls the Beachwood project 'a difficult 20-year campaign'. Medium: the year is Rabbi Chaikin's start; when the Beachwood branch itself began is not stated. Listing address 2480 Beachwood Boulevard.

117702.name: Chabad of Akron & Canton
117702.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'Chabad of Akron-Canton opened in 1981. The Sasonkins arrived in 1989 to serve as shluchim to the Akron-Canton community.' Medium: the CJN (3 Oct 2018, Rabbi Mendel Sasonkin's obituary) says 'In 1989, the couple relocated to Summit County to form Chabad of Akron & Canton', and who ran it from 1981 is not found. Since October 2018 his son Rabbi Moshe Sasonkin directs it. Listing address 599 Pebble Beach Drive.

526300.name: Anshe Sfard Synagogue
526300.note: An older Akron congregation led by Chabad's rabbi since 1995. Cleveland Jewish News (3 Oct 2018): 'Since 1995, he served Anshe Sfard Congregation-Revere Road Synagogue, where Kaila has served as education director.' The CJN (3 July 2014): Rabbi Mendy Sasonkin 'was also spiritual leader of Agudas Achim, an Orthodox synagogue in Canton, from 1990 to 1995 and was named to lead Revere Road Synagogue in 1995.' The CJN (1 July 2020): Rabbi Moshe Sasonkin was appointed 'rabbi at Anshe Sfard Revere Road Synagogue in Bath Township in October 2018'. Its chabad.org listing went up June 6 2007. Now 646 N Revere Road.

613999.name: Hebrew School
613999.note: No start date found: the Hebrew school of Chabad of Akron & Canton (Mrs. Kaila Sasonkin), at Anshe Sfard, 646 N Revere Road. The Sasonkins came in 1989; the Cleveland Jewish News (3 Oct 2018): at Anshe Sfard 'Kaila has served as education director'. Its chabad.org listing went up Dec 18 2007, so it existed by then.

117709.name: Chabad of Cleveland Heights
117709.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'Rabbi Mordechai Mendelson has been director of Chabad of Cleveland Heights since 1984.' Now 3499 Bainbridge Road.

117710.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Solon
117710.note: Cleveland Jewish News (9 Sept 2004): 'the Greenbergs came to Cleveland in July of 1991 with their one-week-old son. Using money they had borrowed from their family, they rented a house in Solon'; 'During that first fall, the Greenbergs held High Holiday services in a nearby Days Inn.'; 'Starting from scratch, the couple built up their Chabad center in a storefront location'; 'Brown brick Chabad of Solon's building officially opened on Sept. 5.' The CJN (3 July 2014): 'Rabbi Zushe and Miriam Greenberg launched the Chabad Jewish Center of Solon in their former Solon home in 1991'; it 'moved to its permanent site at 5570 Harper Road in 2004.'

earlier.where: the Greenbergs' rented house in Solon

118540.name: Friendship Circle
118540.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'Friendship Circle of Cleveland was established in 2003.' The CJN (5 Feb 2004): 'This girls club came about through The Friendship Circle, a group that matches special-needs children with teenagers'; 'Estie Marozov, youth coordinator for The Friendship Circle'. Rabbi Yossi Marozov directs it; now 27900 Gates Mills Boulevard.

658716.name: Chabad's Enrichment Programs
658716.note: No start date found: Rabbi Shmuli Friedman's programs (a department of Chabad of Cleveland), at 25400 Fairmount Blvd. CrownHeights.info (5 Feb 2020, from the Cleveland Jewish News): 'The Friedmans will continue directing the Jewish Learning Institute and Camp Gan Israel, which are currently housed in the former Cleveland Hebrew School building on Fairmount Boulevard'. The Friedmans ran Camp Gan Israel of Beachwood from summer 2008. Its chabad.org listing went up April 2 2008, so it existed by then.

4736058.name: Camp Gan Israel of Beachwood
4736058.note: Cleveland Jewish News (21 Aug 2009): 'Enrollment at Camp Gan Israel of Beachwood more than doubled in its second year, says director Rivky Friedman. Camp Gan Israel of Solon, affiliated with Solon Chabad Jewish Center, opened the sister camp for Beachwood residents using Fuchs Mizrachi School as its base.' So its first summer was 2008. Medium: the CJN (3 July 2014) says it 'was also launched in 2009'. Its chabad.org listing went up June 14 2020. Now at 25400 Fairmount Blvd.

3923569.name: Fromovitz Chabad Center
3923569.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'In 2009, the Fromovitz Adult Jewish Learning Academy opened at the Waxman Chabad Center in Beachwood. Rabbi Moshe and Rivky Gancz are program directors.' The CJN (April 2017): 'Fromovitz Chabad Center Rabbi Moshe Gancz will host a first Seder' at the Waxman Chabad Center, 2479 S. Green Road. Its chabad.org listing went up Jan 25 2018, at its own address, 23711 Chagrin Blvd.

earlier.where: the Waxman Chabad Center, 2479 S. Green Road, Beachwood

1338841.name: Chabad of Oberlin College
1338841.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'Chabad at Oberlin College, led by Rabbi Shlomo and Devorah Elkan, was established in 2010.' Its chabad.org listing went up Oct 28 2010 (Chabad.org news, 19 Nov 2010: 'New Centers Cater to Art Students, Suburbanites'). Rabbi Yisroel Pinson leads it now; 214 W College Street.

2112170.name: Chabad of Downtown Cleveland
2112170.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'Chabad of Downtown, which operates out of a rented office in Cleveland, followed in 2011 under the direction of Rabbi Yossi and Chaya Freedman.' Its chabad.org listing went up Jan 20 2013. Now 1111 Superior Avenue E, Suite 1320.

6892760.name: CYP Cleveland
6892760.note: No start date found: the young professionals arm of Chabad of Downtown Cleveland (2112170, from 2011). CrownHeights.info (27 Jan 2022): Rabbi Yossi Freedman, 'who together with his wife Chaya co-directs Chabad Young Professionals of Cleveland', so it existed by then. Its chabad.org listing went up May 20 2025.

2045594.name: Chabad at CWRU
2045594.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'Chabad at CWRU, which opened in 2012, is run from the home of Rabbi Mendy and Sara Alevsky in University Circle.' Its chabad.org listing went up Nov 23 2012. Now 1524 E 115th Street.

2357326.name: Lyndhurst Chabad Family Center
2357326.note: Cleveland Jewish News (3 July 2014): 'The newest Chabad location in Greater Cleveland is the Chabad Family Center in Lyndhurst, which opened in January. It is led by Rabbi Mendy and Chaya Freedman.' Its chabad.org listing went up Oct 24 2013, before the opening. Now 5120 Ridgebury Blvd.

2842082.name: Chabad of Athens and Ohio University
2842082.note: Cleveland Jewish News (11 Sept 2015): Rabbi Levi Raichik, with his wife Chanee, 'is spearheading the Chabad at Ohio University in Athens'; 'Chabad opened its doors at 100 Morris Ave. in Athens in mid-August during student move-in week.' Its chabad.org listing went up Feb 5 2015. Now 33 N Court Street.

3011242.name: Chabad of the West Side
3011242.note: Cleveland Jewish News (11 Sept 2015): 'Chabad of the West Side, located in Westlake, opened in early August.' Rabbi Mendel and Devorah Jacobs; 'Friday night Shabbat services will be held inside the couple's home at 2951 Canterbury Road in Westlake.' Its chabad.org listing went up July 20 2015. Listing address 4021 Harding Drive, Westlake; the CJN (24 April 2026) places it in Lakewood, with its Jewish Discovery Center (5435870).

earlier.where: the Jacobses' home, 2951 Canterbury Road, Westlake

3547107.name: Chabad at Kent State
3547107.note: Cleveland Jewish News (1 July 2020): Rabbi Moshe Sasonkin 'and his wife, Mussie, had just founded their own Chabad center at Kent State University in Kent in 2017.' Rabbi Berel and Rochel Sasonkin took over in May 2020 ('He and Rochel began the position in May'). Its chabad.org listing went up Jan 30 2017. Now 486 S Marigold Lane.

3596832.name: Twinsburg Chabad
3596832.note: Cleveland Jewish News (15 Aug 2017): 'A Chabad Jewish Center is scheduled to open in Twinsburg and will offer its first services during the High Holy Days.' Rabbi Mendy and Mussie Greenberg; 'This will be the first Jewish institution in Twinsburg.' The CJN's Rosh Hashanah list (19 Sept 2017) has the Twinsburg Chabad Jewish Center at the Twinsburg Community Center. Its chabad.org listing went up March 13 2017. Now 9945 Vail Drive, Suite 2.

5435870.name: The Jewish Discovery Center
5435870.note: Cleveland Jewish News (19 Dec 2021): 'Chabad of the West Side opened its new Jewish Discovery Center Dec. 15 in front of a crowd of Jewish supporters at 15618 Madison Ave., near Wagar Park in Lakewood.' Its chabad.org listing went up March 15 2022.

5333495.name: Chabad Jewish Center of Chagrin Falls
5333495.note: Cleveland Jewish News (25 May 2023, 'Chabad of Chagrin Falls reflects on first nine months'): 'Chabad of Chagrin Falls opened in August 2022', ahead of its first holiday event on Rosh Hashanah; 'Operated by Itzinger and his wife, Simi, out of their home'. The CJN (24 Aug 2022): 'Rabbi Shneur and Simi Itzinger are preparing to open a Chabad in Chagrin Falls.' Its chabad.org listing went up Jan 18 2022. Listing address 100 N Main Street, Suite 100.

6933480.name: Anash Youth Club
6933480.note: CrownHeights.info (17 Aug 2025, 'New Shluchim To Serve The Anash Youth In Cleveland, Ohio'): 'Meet Rabbi Itche and Chaya Chein who together with their daughter Chana are moving out on Shlichus to Cleveland, Ohio.' They will serve the Anash community 'through programs, events and a starting a Youth Club'. Its chabad.org listing went up July 22 2025. Listing address 2479 S Green Rd (the Waxman Chabad Center).

6940306.name: Shaker Chabad
6940306.note: Cleveland Jewish News (24 March 2026): 'Nearly six months after trading the fast pace of New York City for the quieter, tree-lined streets of Shaker Heights, the Mishulovin family of eight is finding its rhythm in Cleveland with the launch of the new Shaker Chabad in Shaker Heights.' Since moving, they have hosted 'a picnic for Rosh Hashanah' (Sept 2025). Its chabad.org listing went up July 22 2025. Chabad had shelved an earlier plan for a Shaker Heights branch (the CJN, 15 March 2001: 'Plans to expand Chabad House of Cleveland to Shaker Heights have been shelved').
